newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's debt down to $28 bln vs $33 bln in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's debt down to $28 bln vs $33 bln in 1995.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler on Saturday said external debt had fallen in 1996, but stressed the need for rescheduling and said the same $2.0 billion would be earmarked for repayments in 1997.
External debt stood at $28.060 billion at the end of December 1996 from $32.585 billion a year earlier.

"As a result of adroit debt management for the first time in over a decade, and without fresh debt rescheduling, this government has succeeded in reversing the trend of rising external debt stock," General Sani Abacha said in his 1997 budget address. He did not give precise details of how the debt had been reduced.
Roughly the same amount, $2.0 billion, has been set aside for external debt servicing for the past five years.

Despite the fall in external debt in 1996, Abacha said the debt profile was unsustainable and stressed the need for relief from the Paris Club of governments which accounts for over 60 percent of the debt.
He said that finalising a Medium Term Economic Strategy (MTES) with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank would be essential before any approach to the Paris Club could be made.
"During 1997 the major focus of Nigeria's relationship with the IMF and World Bank would be accelerated and intensive negotiation and finalisation of the MTES," said Abacha.
